findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge’s (PIC) Certified Food Protection Manger (CFPM) certificate has expired, as of this May. The PIC is scheduled to take their CFPM exam next month. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times food is being prepared or handled.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: The Road Ranger did not have a designated person in charge (PIC) who has knowledge about safe food handling practices present during today’s inspection. Multiple priority and priority foundation violations were observed during today’s inspection. Violations 3, 23, 24, and 28 could all contribute to food-borne illness. Ensure all staff handling and preparing food have food safety education. A follow up inspection will occur on 09/22/25 to ensure priority and priority foundation violations have been corrected.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.[10]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Employees were unable to produce employee reporting agreements. A blank copy will be emailed to the PIC on Monday, 09/15/25. Ensure all employees handling or serving food items read and sign agreements by 09/22/25.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT (for all items): The following temperature control for food safety items were observed without date marking:
1) Creamer, whole milk, and half and half in the creamer dispenser
2) Pizza sauce in the prep cooler.- CORRECTED. The employee who prepares pizza arrived and marked the sauce with the day it was removed from its container. 
All TCS items must contain date marking. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. Items must be used or discarded within 7 days,
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Paperwork (verification and procedures) for time as public health control (TAC) used for pizza was unable to be presented to the inspector at this time. Facilities using TAC must have verifiable procedures and written records available at the inspectors request. Inspector will return to the facility on 09/22 to verify TAC paperwork with PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(A) Time as a Public Health Control. (A) Except as specified under (D) of this section, if time without temperature control is used as the public health control for a working supply of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD before cooking, or for READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is displayed or held for sale or service: (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and made available to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY upon request that specify:  (a) Methods of compliance with Subparagraphs (B)(1)-(4) or (C)(1)-(5) of this section.; and (b) Methods of compliance with § 3-501.14 for FOOD that is prepared, cooked, and refrigerated before time is used as a public health control. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed engine lubricant and coolant being stored over prepackaged juices and soda in the facilities dry storage area (near the walk in cooler). Food items cannot be stored underneath toxic substances. Ensure toxic substances are stored away or underneath food items to prevent the contamination of RTE (ready to eat) food items.
findings.citation_text: 7-301.11 Separation. POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple cold holding units missing ambient air thermometers in the following locations:
1) Standing cooler #1 (dairy)
2) Standing deli cooler
3) Standing double door cooler in the pizza prep room
Cold holding units intended for the storage of TCS food items must contain an easily readable ambient thermometer in the warmest part of the cooler. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the aforementioned locations.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed single service food boats in the pizza prep area to be stored with their food contact surface facing up. CORRECTED- Food Handler inverted the trays. Ensure food contact surfaces are protected from contamination by storing them under a covering, or in an inverted position.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C}

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Single service articles (cups, lids, to go containers, and food trays) were observed to be stored on the floor in the dry storage area of the triple sink room, as well as the pizza prep room. Single service containers must be stored at least 6 inches above the ground to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the gaskets of several standing coolers to be in disrepair. Coolers are in the following locations:
1) Standing cooler #8 (Red Bull)
2) Standing cooler #9 (Celsius)
3) Standing cooler #11 (Pepsi)
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Gaskets should be repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets on the creamer dispenser to be soiled with mold accumulation. Ensure gaskets and all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the caulking around the hand washing sink (in the triple sink room) to contain a biofilm, and to be separating from the wall. Clean and replace the caulking to prevent the growth and harborage of microorganisms. This repair will also provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIRD REPEAT: The floor under the milk storage shelving in the walk in cooler was observed to contain a significant amount of soil debris and splash. Ensure the physical facility is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Staff members were unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates at the inspector’s request. Ensure that all employees who handle or prepare RTE food have a Food Handler’s Certificate available at the inspector’s request. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No certified food protection manager (CFM) was present during this inspection. The facility needs to be under direct, on-site supervision of a CFM during all times of food preparation and service. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff and scheduled to cover all necessary shifts.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Whole milk, half & half, and creamer in dispenser were without date marks. CORRECTED- Dairy products were labeled to indicate when they were opened.
Pizza sauce in the prep cooler was observed without a date-marking. PIC indicated that sauce usually lasts 2-3 days. Ensure foods that will remain in the facility for more than 24 hours are labeled with the date they were opened or prepared. CORRECTED- Pizza sauce was labeled with the date it was prepared.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18 A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A spray bottle of red liquid was observed in the pizza prep kitchen without any label. Discussion with staff determined that it is a different kind of quat sanitizer. Ensure chemical containers are labeled to indicate their contents. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the spray bottle.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility’s probe thermometers were observed to read 20F when placed in ice water. CORRECTED- Demonstrated thermometer calibration and discussed the process with PIC. Thermometers were recalibrated. Verify thermometer calibration regularly to ensure accuracy.
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Boxes of of foods were observed stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer. Store foods at least 6 inches above the ground to protect from contamination.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Single service articles (cups, lids, gloves) were observed stored on the ground in the storage area near the walk-in cooler, in the pizza prep kitchen, and in the dish/dry storage area. Store single service containers at least 6 inches above the ground.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Gaskets on the creamer dispenser observed to be soiled with mold accumulation. Clean gaskets more frequently to prevent mold accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 2nd REPEAT: Floor under milk storage shelving in the cooler was soiled with general buildup and splash. Clean the floor under shelving in the walk-in cooler and throughout the facility as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Caulk dish area handwashing sink to the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Whole milk, half & half, and creamer in dispenser were without date marks. Employee noted product is typically used within 1 to 2 days. Product that PIC knows was placed in the dispenser yesterday were labeled accordingly. Products that a timeline could not be established will be discarded at the end of the day today.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18 A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single service cups, paper boats, and to-go containers observed stored on the floor in the pizza kitchen. Store single service containers at least 6 inches above the ground.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Quat test strips have been water damaged and are no longer effective. Get fresh test strips and ensure they are available to monitor sanitizer concentration.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Food accumulation observed on the interior of the microwave. Clean microwave.
2) Gaskets on the creamer dispenser observed to be soiled with mold accumulation. Clean gaskets.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Leak observed from the faucet of the 3 compartment sink. Repair leak.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; and (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1. Handsink in the ware washing/back storage area was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin and along upper surfaces. Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.
2. Floor under milk storage shelving in the cooler was soiled with general buildup and splash. Clean the floor under shelving in the walk-in cooler and throughout the facility as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulk dish area handwashing sink to the wall. 
2) Ensure walls around the mop sink are sealed to the floor (caulk or base trim). 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler certificate could not be located for one of the two employee working at this time. Certificate could not be located for the other primary employee who was not present during this inspection. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees that handle food.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at time of inspection did not have proof of food manager certification. Ensure that enough staff have food manager certifications to allow for a designated person in charge with a CFM to be present during all hours of operation.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink in the men’s restroom. Handwashing sign was provided. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwasing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Hotdogs and sausages on right roller grill were observed with surface temperatures ranging from 124F-138F. Internal temperatures for two products were noted to be 126F and 132F. Roller grill items were said to be heated within the last hour and were possibly moved up to front rollers too soon. The front rollers were also at too low of a setting and needed to be adjusted. Products in question were reheated during inspection above 165F prior to placing back on front hot holding rollers.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Portions of egg, sausage crumbles, and gravy in the bottom of the pizza prep cooler were observed without date marks. All products were discarded.
2. Whole milk, half & half, and creamer in dispenser were without date marks. Employee noted product is typically used within 1 to 2 days and provided a date mark for discard of 11/29 for product to be replaced the following business day. Whole milk was replaced during inspection and properly dated. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1. Handsink in the ware washing/back storage area was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin and along upper surfaces. Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.
2. Floor under milk storage shelving in the cooler was soiled with general buildup and splash. Clean the floor under shelving in the walk-in cooler and throughout the facility as needed. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open packages of diced ham and sausage crumbles were without date marks in the pizza prep cooler. Packages were opened the day prior and this morning. Date marks were provided.
Except as specified in ¶¶ (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302. Food thermometer used for taking internal temperatures recently broke. A spare thermometer was located but was unable to be calibrated. The needle was broken and would not adjust correctly when checked with ice point method. New food thermometers will be purchased.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Flats containing canned gravy and pizza sauce were observed on the floor in the pizza kitchen. Crates were provided to store flats up off the floor. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-502.13 Tubes on bulk creamer were not cut at an angle for two of the products. Dispensing tubes were cut to be at an angle. 
Bulk container dispensing tubes shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Box of single service cups was observed on the floor in the back storage area. Crate was provided to store cups up off the floor.
 Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Cabinets beneath the fountain soda machine were cracked and damaged. Provide repairs so cabinets are smooth and easily cleanable.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification had to leave prior to conclusion of inspection. The person left in charge only had a food handler certification. Additional staff with food manager certifications are needed. Ensure that enough staff have food manager certifications to allow for a designated person in charge with a CFM to be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 PIC rinsed hands at 3 part sink after handling a chemical bottle. Handwashing at designated handwashing sinks was discussed. Ensure that hands are only washed at handsinks. If hands need to be rinsed, then hands should be properly washed regardless of the next task that will occur.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink in the ware washing/back storage area. Maintain handwashing signage at all designated handsinks. Handwashing signs were provided for management to post where needed. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwasing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket at food service area was observed at 0ppm quat despite being made within the last few hours. The solution was relatively clean. The wiping cloth in use may have absorbed chemical out of solution. The solution was remade and observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain solutions from SuperSan dispenser at 150-400ppm as directed, and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Pizza slicer was observed soiled and resting on a wet paper towel on the top ledge of the prep cooler. Slicer was taken to ware washing area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Box containing hinged food containers was observed on the floor under the prep table in the pizza kitchen. Box was placed up on a shelf for proper storage. 
Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit available for use was severely water damage. Kit was discarded. Extra test strips were available for use from Subway. Additional test kits would be purchased. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Handsink in the ware washing/back storage area was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin and along upper surfaces. Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Whipped topping did not have a date mark on the in-use open pouch at the drink counter. Manager stated it was likely opened the day prior. Date mark of 10/25 was added to the pouch. 
Topping is good at ambient temperature for 5 days based on product information. Manager was advised to make sure the pouches are dated to ensure use in 5 days or less. 

In-use creamers in refrigerated dispenser were not dated. Four creamers were opened the day prior and one was just placed in the dispenser this morning. Proper date marks were written on the metal containers in the dispenser.
Cold foods that requite time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be properly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
750. 120 & 250 - Pizza at hot holding area was observed with surface temperature below 130°F. Manager noted the pizzas are typically pulled for discard w/in 2hrs if product is not already sold. Time is not currently being tracked for pizzas. Track time for pizzas and serve or discard w/in 4hrs or less.  

Hot TCS foods shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 135°F/above at all times during storage, display and service unless time control is used.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.230 - Infrared thermometer was available for checking temperatures. Manager noted his stem thermometer was given to Subway for use. Obtain another food thermometer for monitoring food temperatures during heating and holding. 

 A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Packages of sausages and tornados were out on the prep table in the pizza kitchen. Items were in the process of thawing. Some products were still very frozen, while others were relatively thawed. Surface temperature of one package of sausages was at 45°F. Manager placed all products in the bottom of the pizza cooler to finish thawing.

TCS foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Tubes of bulk creamers and milk in the dispenser at the drink counter were cut straight across resulting in incidental creamer and milk remaining in the tubes between uses. GM was advised to cut the tubes at an angle to allow for drainage of incidental creamer and milk between uses. GM cut the tubes at an angle during the inspection.

Food shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Maintenance worker was unable to properly wash hands at back area handsink due to the absence of soap. Hands were rinsed and then dried with paper towels. Soap dispenser recently fell off the wall and had not yet been replaced. Employee. re-installed the dispenser during the inspection. GM was advised to reiterate the important for proper handwashing with all staff.

Maintain soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Proper technique must always be used when washing hands. Also, maintain handsinks and related fixtures in a clean and in good repair.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) cookie spatula on top of oven (food debris);
B) behind/around soda nozzles (buildup);   and
C) inside microwave at hot food counter (splash).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Counters under/behind equipment in food service area were soiled with buildup of dust and/or general debris. 

Clean under/behind equipment as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) The open air display cooler holding Country Fresh Meats does not have a conspicuously placed thermometer. Provide a thermometer and then monitor this cooler. See notes in General Comments for details.  All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Facility is observed using a cloth with spray bottle for counter wiping. Discussed using a spray bottle with a paper towel or using the wet wiping cloth in conjuncture with a sani-bucket. Cloth should be kept in sani-bucket solution in-between uses. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e  The square spout containers of the self-service soda display are observed soiled with syrup accumulation. Clean the underside of this soda dispensing machine. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed mouse droppings in the cabinets holding concentrated tea and that cabinet located to the left. Facility has monthly pest control service (McCloud Pest Control out of Pekin). There were very few droppings present. It is recommended that facility contact pest control specialist and have spot service conducted. Cleaned during the inspection. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed the spray bottle on the display counter by the handsink to not have a label. Bottle contained quat sanitizing solution. Labeled during the inspection. The bottle was also just over 200ppm Quat. Solution should be 200ppm Quat. Make sure that contents are tested to insure proper concentration. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-110g REPEAT: There are a number of David's Baked Goods available for grab-and-go service at the cash register. These foods do not have proper labeling. Make sure that ingredients and manufacturing information are available should a customer request the information. Contact David's, they may have  sticker labeling already available for commercial repackaging. Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed chipboard boats being used to hold single-service packets of salt and pepper. Cease use of this absorbent material and switch to a material that is nonabsorbent, smooth, and easily cleanable. The container should be able to be run through the ware washing process. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
